proposal.thesis: Arista beat Q2 2026 hard (revenue $3.036B vs $2.874B est, first-ever $3B quarter, +37.7% YoY per the company's own release -- the bundle digest's 51.4% YoY figure for the same quarter conflicts with this and I am using the sourced number) and raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $12.6B (+40% YoY), reported 2026-08-04 (WebSearch: Yahoo Finance, BigGo, investors.arista.com). EPS beat by +15.2%, the largest of a 4-quarter accelerating beat streak (+5.0%/+8.2%/+7.7%/+15.2%, news_and_catalysts.earnings_surprises). The reported growth is currently supply-capped, not demand-capped: deferred revenue backlog reached $6.2B and multiyear purchase commitments rose from $3.6B to $9.7B YoY as the company locks up wafer/optics/memory supply against demand it cannot yet ship (WebSearch, industry coverage of the print, not in bundle). Fundamentals are clean: net cash (-0.5x net debt/EBITDA), TTM operating margin improving to 43.87% (+1.43pp YoY) despite slight gross-margin compression, inventory-to-revenue improving (83.52% vs 93.39% a year ago -- supply discipline, not overbuild), $2.69B FCF YTD. Valuation is reasonable for the growth rate (fwd P/E 38.3x vs 40.7% forward revenue growth, fwd_pe_to_growth 0.94, flagged cheap_vs_growth by the data) versus NET/CRWD/RBRK, all flagged rich_vs_growth at 5.6-6.0x. Chart (viewed) shows a clean uptrend with the post-earnings gap now in a tight multi-session pullback holding above the rising 20-DMA -- the day-after-first-pullback entry, not a chase of the gap day.
catalysts: Backlog conversion: $6.2B deferred revenue + $9.7B multiyear purchase commitments (up from $3.6B YoY) convert to recognized revenue as wafer/optics/memory supply eases (WebSearch, industry coverage of the 2026-08-04 print)
4th consecutive EPS beat (surprise +15.2%, largest of the streak) and FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $12.6B (+40% YoY), reported 2026-08-04
Etherlink AI-fabric switch adoption past 100 cumulative customers, expanding networking's share of AI-cluster capex (WebSearch, 2026-08-04 earnings call)
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive: SPY $770.56 is 9.9% above its 200-DMA and 3.1% above its 50-DMA, up 2.9% over 1 month, regime_hint 4/5. momentum_health is healthy (no factor-unwind haircut). VIX 15.4 and falling, no active market_events flags. sector_rotation_30d shows the AI-infrastructure complex (hyperscaler_enablers +37.9pp, semi_equipment +13.4pp, networking +11.9pp) re-accelerating even as cybersecurity -- home to the richest-valued alternatives I passed on today -- decelerates (-6.2pp). This supports adding one honest, reasonably-valued new position at normal size.
proposal.risk_map: This fails if: (1) absolute valuation (EV/EBITDA 54.5x) gets punished on any stumble despite the growth-adjusted multiple being reasonable; (2) gross margin compression (63.52% vs 64.10% TTM) continues and stops being offset by opex leverage, undermining the operating-margin-improving read; (3) a large hyperscaler customer (high customer concentration per stack_cards) delays or cancels capacity, since the backlog thesis depends on that demand being real and sticky; (4) the market reads the supply-constraint narrative as a genuine growth ceiling rather than pent-up demand, given the stock is already +50% over 3 months and much of the good news may be priced in. Early tell: a daily close below the $196.41 anchored VWAP on above-average volume, or a specific hyperscaler-customer delay headline.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Analysts rate ANET strong_buy (mean 1.27, 27 analysts, mean target $241.82, +22.2% upside) and already know Arista delivered a 4th straight EPS beat and raised FY26 guidance to $12.6B -- the beat-and-raise itself is priced in (stock +50% over 3 months, rel_strength_3m +40.5%). MY VIEW: what the tape has not fully processed is that reported growth is currently supply-capped, not demand-capped. MECHANISM: deferred revenue backlog reached $6.2B and multiyear purchase commitments rose from $3.6B to $9.7B YoY (WebSearch, industry coverage of the 2026-08-04 print, not in bundle) precisely because Arista can sell more than it can ship; sell-side models typically extrapolate off the reported revenue trajectory, so a backlog growing faster than recognized revenue means the reported growth rate understates the real demand curve, and each unit of freed supply (management guided the industry stays tight into 2028, so this normalizes gradually) converts near dollar-for-dollar into revenue against an already-secured order book. RESOLUTION: the Q3 FY2026 print (~November, outside this trade's horizon) will show whether the backlog kept building or started converting, but the observable near-term test is whether the current post-earnings base holds and extends toward the $241 analyst mean target over the next several weeks.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: Any interim disclosure showing the $6.2B deferred-revenue backlog shrinking quarter-over-quarter, or TTM gross margin falling meaningfully below the current 63.52% level (already down from 64.10% a year ago) due to elevated component costs without an offsetting operating-margin gain.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below the anchored VWAP support at $196.41 on above-average volume, giving back the 2026-08-04 post-earnings breakout.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If ANET has not closed above $215 (roughly halfway to the $241.82 analyst mean target) within 30 trading days of entry (by ~2026-09-26), the post-print drift isn't developing -- exit and rotate.

proposal.risk_desk_note: Falsifiers are genuinely specific and observable (deferred-revenue backlog shrinking QoQ, close below $196.41 anchored VWAP on above-average volume, close above $215 within 30 trading days) — passes checklist item 1. Sourcing diligence is unusually strong: I cross-checked every bundle-verifiable fig
proposal.sizing_note: risk-clamped from $116 to $116: 1.00% risk budget ($10) / 8.7% stop
